rows.grounds: reduplicated pronoun indicating any desired result
fused form: phalati + asandehaḥ + tu + aprayatnena; notes effortless fruition

items.question: What outcome follows from an act performed without effort in this practice?
premises: Any desired result can bear fruit without doubt.
Such fruition can occur even without deliberate effort.
The act in question is already accomplished.
items.inference: A properly accomplished act yields its intended result effortlessly and certainly.
uncertainties: The exact referent of kṛtam (ritual act or general deed) is not specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Whatever is done bears fruit without doubt, even without effort.

rows.grounds: state of identification with the deity

items.question: What two attainments arise when mantra practice reaches its successful fulfillment?
premises: The practitioner obtains the state of the deity.
Success in the mantra arises.
Both outcomes are presented together as results.
items.inference: Mantra accomplishment brings both identification with the deity and mantra-success.
uncertainties: Whether devatābhāvam is cause or co-result of mantrasiddhiḥ is not explicitly stated.
items.plain_english: One attains the state of the deity, and mantra-success arises.

items.question: How do obstacles behave in the presence of an accomplished practitioner?
premises: Obstacles flee upon seeing the practitioner.
Elephants flee upon seeing a lion.
The verse draws an explicit comparison between these two cases.
items.inference: Obstacles disperse before the accomplished practitioner as elephants flee from a lion.
uncertainties: The verse implies but does not name the practitioner as the object seen by obstacles.
items.plain_english: Obstacles flee on seeing him, just as elephants flee on seeing a lion.

items.question: What condition befalls one who lacks the power to repel obstacles?
premises: Someone is afflicted by all obstacles.
A fawn is afflicted by tigers.
The verse compares the afflicted person to the fawn.
items.inference: Without protective power, one is overwhelmed by obstacles like a fawn by tigers.
uncertainties: The subject of vādhyate is implied rather than explicitly named.
items.plain_english: And he is afflicted by all obstacles, just as a fawn is afflicted by tigers.

rows.grounds: by means of beads or gems used for counting
the matrix of letters/powers; kept as technical term

items.question: In what two modes can the mātṛkā be constituted during mantra practice?
premises: The mātṛkā may be fashioned with beads.
The mātṛkā may be imagined.
The mātṛkā may also be unimagined.
items.inference: The mātṛkā can be engaged either through bead-supported construction or without mental construction.
uncertainties: The precise contrast between kalpitā and akalpitā in this ritual context is compressed.
items.plain_english: The mātṛkā may be fashioned with beads, imagined, or unimagined.

rows.grounds: one most skilled in mantra knowledge

items.question: How should the most skilled mantra practitioner perform the counting of recitation?
premises: Counting is prescribed for mantra practice.
The counting may proceed in forward and reverse order.
The best knower of mantra is the agent of this counting.
items.inference: The foremost mantra practitioner should count the recitation in both forward and reverse order.
items.plain_english: The best knower of mantra should count in forward and reverse order.

rows.grounds: a count of one hundred thousand
using a ruby bead or ruby beads

items.question: What difference in recitation value is assigned to ordinary beads versus ruby beads?
premises: Recitation with beads is measured as a hundred thousand.
Recitation with ruby is declared endless.
The verse states these valuations explicitly.
items.inference: Using ruby beads is taught to confer an immeasurably greater recitation value than ordinary beads.
uncertainties: Whether māṇikyā refers to a single ruby bead or ruby material is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: With beads it is said to be a hundred thousand; with ruby it is said to be endless.

rows.grounds: by means of fifty repetitions or beads

items.question: What level of accomplishment is declared to result from a count of fifty?
premises: A count of fifty is specified.
All-success is declared as the result.
The declaration is addressed to the Lady of Kula.
items.inference: Even a count of fifty is taught to yield complete accomplishment.
uncertainties: The unit counted by pañcāśadbhiḥ (beads, repetitions, or cycles) is implied by context.
items.plain_english: O Lady of Kula, with fifty, all-success is declared.

rows.grounds: fused compound indicating purposes of stambhana and ākarṣaṇa

items.question: Which finger is renowned for use in acts of immobilizing and attracting?
premises: The little finger is named.
It is associated with immobilizing and attracting.
It is described as well renowned for this purpose.
items.inference: The little finger is the traditionally praised finger for immobilizing and attracting rites.
uncertainties: The exact ritual application of stambhana and ākarṣaṇa is not detailed here.
items.plain_english: The little finger is well renowned for immobilizing and attracting.

items.question: What concluding offering should follow mantra recitation performed in a steady posture?
premises: The practitioner is seated firmly.
The practitioner has completed chanting.
An offering with water is to be made to the Goddess.
items.inference: After steady seated recitation, one should offer water to the Goddess.
uncertainties: What exactly is offered together with water is not specified beyond sodakam.
items.plain_english: Seated firmly, after chanting, one should then offer it with water to the Goddess.

items.question: Which form of recitation is ranked highest within the threefold classification of japa?
premises: Recitation is declared to be threefold.
Mental recitation is named as the highest.
This teaching is addressed to the Goddess.
items.inference: Among the three kinds of japa, mental recitation is taught as the highest.
uncertainties: The other two kinds of japa are not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, recitation is declared to be threefold, and mental recitation is the highest.

rows.grounds: mixed with proper letters and improper elements

items.question: Why does a mantra mixed with proper and improper elements fail to accomplish its aim?
premises: A mantra may be joined with letter and non-letter elements.
Such a mantra is identified as the subject.
The verse states that this mantra does not succeed.
items.inference: A mantra corrupted by improper admixture fails to achieve success.
uncertainties: The exact technical meaning of akṣara versus akṣara in this compound is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: A mantra that is mixed with proper and improper elements does not succeed.
